issues: Experimental nanoparticles were near-equiatomic, not equiatomic; only the primary simulations used an equiatomic composition.
The 45-minute limit was imposed because the nanoparticles continuously evolved, while IR interference was handled by returning to 298 K for EDS.
Phase separation is enabled kinetically by diffusion but tends toward a thermodynamic equilibrium stabilized by surface-energy effects, so the mechanism is not purely kinetically controlled.
Au/Cu evaporation caused a transient 22% size reduction at 973 K, while concurrent coalescence widened the size distribution; a general reduction in average size is imprecise.
Significant segregation begins mainly in coalesced particles at 773-873 K and becomes universal with evaporation at 973 K, not immediately above 673 K.
The claimed size dependence is contradicted within the simulated 2.1-5.2 nm range, where similar thermal trends were found.
Au self-diffusivity and STEM-EDS shape/composition evolution were complementary rather than a single simultaneous measurement.
